The device consists of commercially available optical components such as polarizers and mirrors.
The device is designed as a 12-port structure with the cloaking and image projection functionalities achieved through the use of orthogonal polarizations.
The vertically polarized light is bent 90 degrees by the polarizers, while the horizontally polarized light passes straight through, enabling the reconstruction of the scene behind the cloak.
The remaining 50% of the incident light is used for image projection, allowing the display of information in any desired region of the cloak structure.
As the view angle increases from 0 to 4 degrees, the reconstructed scene starts to degrade due to the loss of information and incorrect positioning of the image.
The device can be used to realize transparent electronics and see-through displays, such as in cellphones, smart glasses, automotive applications, and augmented reality technologies.
The use of commercially available optical components makes the device easier to implement and a significant step towards practical applications.
The device handles the trade-off between cloaking and image projection by utilizing the orthogonal polarizations of light to achieve both functionalities simultaneously.
The current device has limitations in terms of view angle and image quality, which may require further improvements in the optical design.

The key innovation is the integration of invisibility cloaking and image projection capabilities in a single device, opening up new possibilities for transparent electronics and augmented reality applications.
The device demonstrates a novel approach that has not been explored in previous works on invisibility cloaks and transparent displays.
The experimental demonstration of the device validates the proposed mechanism and architecture for combining cloaking and image projection functionalities.

The device provides a practical and cost-effective solution for transparent displays and see-through electronics, compared to previous approaches that relied on specialized materials or optical elements.
The device's ability to project images in any desired region of the cloak structure, including the middle of neighboring areas, is a unique capability.
The device's performance is analyzed in terms of the view angle dependence, providing insights into the limitations and potential improvements required for practical applications.
